messages.content: 我想在聖荷西附近的Walmart買蘋果、米飯和12罐瓶裝水。請顯示產品資訊和庫存情況。

function.name: walmart_purchase
function.description: Retrieve information of items from Walmart including stock availability. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

product_list.description: Items to be purchased listed in an array.

pack_size.description: Size of the product pack if applicable. The size of the array should be equal to product_list. Default is not use it if not specified.

message.reasoning:
The user wants to buy apples, rice, and 12 cans of bottled water near San Jose Walmart. They want product info and stock status. We need to call the function walmart_purchase with location "San Jose" or "nearby" and product list ["apples", "rice", "bottled water"] and pack_size maybe [12] for bottled water? Actually they want 12 cans of bottled water. So product_list includes "apples", "rice", "bottled water". pack_size array should match product_list length. For apples and rice, no pack size needed. For bottled water, pack_size 12. But pack_size array length must equal product_list length. So we can provide pack_size: [null, null, 12] or maybe [0,0,12]? The function signature says pack_size?: number[]. The default is not use it if not specified. But we need to specify pack_size for bottled water. We could set pack_size: [1,1,12] but apples and rice might be per unit. But the function expects array length equal to product_list. So we can set pack_size: [1,1,12]. Or we can set pack_size: [null,null,12] but type is number[]. So null not allowed. So we set [1,1,12]. That indicates pack size for each product. For apples and rice, pack size 1. For bottled water, 12.

We also need location: "San Jose" or "nearby". The function expects loc: string. We'll give "San Jose".

Thus call function.
